cards.name: shared_temporary_and_across_compute_uncompute_pairs
cards.identity: Normalize h-ccx-h to ccz so the circuit is a classical reversible op list over {x, cx, ccx/ccz}. Symbolically simulate it: every wire w at time t carries an ANF (GF(2) polynomial) P_t(w) in the input variables (ancillas pinned to 0). For a pair of CCZ/CCX gates g_i (earlier, position p) and g_j (later, position q>p) whose control wires carry the SAME unordered pair of ANFs at their own times, {P_p(c1), P_p(c2)} = {P_q(d1), P_q(d2)}, replace them by ONE temporary AND held across [p,q]: at p, and_compute(c1,c2 -> a) on a fresh clean ancilla a [4 T, Gidney gadget: |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; then cz(a, target_i) (or cx(a,target_i) for ccx); the ancilla is left alive and untouched through [p,q]; at q, cz(a, target_j) / cx(a, target_j); immediately after q, and_uncompute(a) = H(a), measure a in X basis, classically controlled CZ(c1,c2) fix-up [0 T]. Generalize to maximal equivalence CLASSES of CCZs with the same control-ANF pair: k gates in a class cost one 4-T AND plus k cz/cx, i.e. 4 T per class instead of 4 T per gate. Ancilla lifetimes are the spans of the classes; spans that overlap get distinct ancillas (<= depth-of-overlap many, each clean in/out).
cards.correctness: (1) The circuit is Hadamard-free once h-ccx-h is folded to ccz, so it is a classical reversible permutation and the ANF of each wire is exact and canonical (ANF is a unique normal form, so ANF equality is a sound test for 'the two gates' control wires hold the same Boolean values on EVERY input', which is the only thing the shared AND needs; it does NOT require the control wires to be left unwritten in between, which is what the existing rule demands). (2) Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with 4 T and no extra relative phase; while a holds x&y, cz(a,z) acts as ccz(x,y,z) and cx(a,z) as ccx(x,y,z) on every basis state, so each class member is reproduced exactly. (3) Because the control ANFs are equal at p and at q, the SAME value x&y is correct at every member's position, even though the control wires were rewritten and restored in between (in the ripple-carry adder MAJ_i and UMA_i see identical carry/bit values). (4) The measurement-based uncompute returns a to |0> and its classically controlled CZ(c1,c2) fix-up cancels the measurement-induced phase, giving the same unitary on every measurement branch with the same constant c_m (phase consistency) -- this is exactly the relaxed contract already verified for the single-gate version of the gadget. (5) Ancillas are clean in and out, so the relaxed spec check applies unchanged.
cards.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit that is Hadamard-free after folding every h(q) ccx(.,.,q) h(q) / h-cz-h pattern into ccz (adder_6: all 22 h's are in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams), containing >= 2 ccz/ccx gates, such that symbolic ANF simulation finds at least one equivalence class of >= 2 ccz/ccx gates with identical unordered control-ANF pairs AND the targets of the members are not themselves inputs to the shared AND inside the span (checked: target wire of a member must not be one of the two control wires of the class, and the class's control ANFs must be unchanged at every member position -- guaranteed by construction). Fires only if the number of classes is strictly less than the number of ccz/ccx gates.
cards.expected_effect: adder_6 is a 6-bit ripple-carry (Cuccaro-style) adder with 2n-1 = 11 Toffoli-level gates: n-1 = 5 carry-compute Toffolis in the MAJ sweep, their 5 mirror-image partners in the UMA sweep (identical control values by construction), and 1 unpaired carry-out Toffoli. The current book pays 4 T per gate (11 x 4 = 44) because each compute/uncompute partner is separated by control-wire writes that are later undone. ANF matching pairs them, giving 6 AND classes -> 6 x 4 = 24 T; the 11 ccz's become 6 and_compute + 11 cz + 6 measured uncompute (0 T). Extra cost: at most 2-3 live clean ancillas instead of 1 (the carry spans nest), and ~6 extra cx/cz; T-count 44 -> 24, i.e. 4n T, the Gidney figure, and below pyzx's 47 and TKET's 59.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND with measurement-based uncompute); control-value matching via algebraic normal form as in phase-polynomial/parity-network analyses (Amy-Maslov-Mosca; Cuccaro et al. quant-ph/0410184 for the MAJ/UMA mirror structure).

cards.name: adder_spec_recognition_gidney_carry_chain_rebuild
cards.identity: Whole-circuit SPECIFICATION recognition plus known-optimal rebuild, not gate pairing. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram back to ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams), leaving an op list over {x, cx, ccx} only: a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire carries an ANF in the input variables x_0..x_13 (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). Let O_w be the final ANF of wire w. (3) Pattern-match the output map against the ripple-carry addition specification: search for an ordered pair of index lists A=(p_0..p_{n-1}), B=(q_0..q_{n-1}) (plus an optional carry-in wire and carry-out wire) such that, writing a_i = x_{p_i}, b_i = x_{q_i}, and the carry recurrence C_0 = c_in, C_{i+1} = a_i b_i + C_i(a_i + b_i), the final ANFs satisfy O_{p_i} = a_i (register A restored), O_{q_i} = a_i + b_i + C_i (sums in register B), O_{carryout} = x_{carryout} + C_n, and O_w = x_w on every other wire. The match is driven, not brute-forced: candidate B wires are those whose ANF has the form (linear part) + (higher-degree part), the degree of the higher part fixes i, and the linear part names a_i, b_i; A and the carry wires follow. (4) If the match succeeds, discard the whole matched segment and emit Gidney's temporary-AND ripple-carry adder on the SAME wires: for i = 0..n-1, cx(a_i -> b_i), cx(a_i -> t_i-1 or c_in), and_compute(b_i, k_i -> anc_i) [4 T, |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>] where k_i is the running carry wire, cx(anc_i -> running carry); after the forward sweep write the carry-out, then run the sweep in reverse, each and_uncompute(anc_i) = H, X-basis measurement, classically-controlled CZ on its two factor wires [0 T], restoring every ancilla to |0> and every A wire to a_i, and finish the sum CXs. Cost: exactly one 4-T AND gadget per carry, n (or n-1 with c_in = 0) gadgets total, no other non-Clifford gate.
cards.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form for Boolean functions, so step (2)-(3) is a sound and complete decision procedure for 'this Hadamard-free circuit computes exactly the ripple-carry sum on these wires': the circuit is a permutation (only x/cx/ccx after folding, and h-ccx-h on the target is literally ccz, so folding is an identity), hence each output wire's value is a polynomial in the inputs and ANF equality is equality of functions on ALL 2^14 inputs. The replacement is verified against that same specification: Gidney's construction computes the identical carry recurrence C_{i+1} = a_i b_i + C_i(a_i+b_i) = a_i + (a_i+b_i)(a_i+C_i) and the identical sums, so output ANFs agree wire by wire. Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x&y> exactly (4 T, no residual relative phase), and while anc holds x&y a cx(anc -> z) acts as ccx(x,y;z) on every basis state. Measurement-based uncompute is applied at a point where the gadget's two factor wires still hold their original values BY CONSTRUCTION (the rebuild chooses the schedule, so no ANF-matching of pre-existing gate pairs is needed -- this is what the earlier shared-AND card could not get on this input): H + X-basis measurement collapses anc to |0> and the classically-controlled CZ(factor1, factor2) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m (x&y)} phase, so every branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m and sum |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). All ancillas are clean in and out, so the relaxed specification check applies unchanged. Global phase only.
cards.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit that (a) becomes Hadamard-free after folding all h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h trigrams, i.e. consists only of x, cx, ccx, and (b) whose end-of-circuit ANF map satisfies the ripple-carry pattern of step (3) for some n >= 3 with disjoint A, B wire lists, an optional carry-in wire holding 0 or a variable, an optional carry-out wire, and identity on all remaining wires. Fires once, on the whole circuit (or on the maximal prefix-to-suffix segment between the first and last ccx if Cliffords outside it are untouched). Fires only if the number of AND gadgets required (n, or n-1 when the carry-in is a pinned 0) is strictly less than the current number of ccx/ccz gates, so it can never increase T. Does NOT fire on mult_4 / mcx_10 / modred_21 (their ANFs are bilinear products or a single n-fold monomial, not the carry recurrence), so the existing accepted rules keep those rows.
cards.expected_effect: adder_6 has 11 ccx (2n-1 for n = 6), which the current book lowers to 11 AND gadgets = 44 T because each gate's controls are written and restored between it and its mirror partner (ANF class matching found 10 classes for 11 gates, so no sharing). Recognizing the circuit as a 6-bit ripple-carry adder and rebuilding it with Gidney's schedule needs one AND per carry: 6 gadgets (5 if the carry-in wire is a pinned clean 0) = 24 T (20 T), i.e. the 4n Gidney figure. All 11 ccx and all 22 h disappear; the replacement has ~26-30 cx/x, 6 and_compute, 6 measured and_uncompute (0 T), and 5-6 extra clean ancillas (14 -> ~19-20 qubits; T drops first in the lexicographic order, so the qubit increase is acceptable). Result 24 T (possibly 20) vs current 44, and well below pyzx 47 / TKET 59 / BQSKit 77.
cards.source: C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (temporary logical-AND, measurement-based uncompute, 4n-T n-bit adder); Cuccaro, Draper, Kutin, Moulton, quant-ph/0410184 (ripple-carry MAJ/UMA specification); ANF / algebraic-normal-form canonicity as used in reversible-circuit equivalence checking (Amy, Maslov, Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization').

cards.name: xag_multiplicative_complexity_resynthesis
cards.identity: Function-level resynthesis of any Hadamard-free classical segment through an XOR-AND-inverter graph (XAG), paying 4 T per AND node and 0 T for every XOR/inverter. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram into ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams); the segment is then an op list over {x, cx, ccx} = a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire w gets its output ANF O_w in the input variables (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). No pattern library, no adder template. (3) Build an XAG for the whole output map by sequential AND extraction over the set S of ALREADY AVAILABLE signals (initially the input variables, i.e. the GF(2)-linear span L(S) of the live wires): repeatedly search for a product g*h, with g,h in L(S) (candidate linear forms taken from the supports appearing in the remaining ANFs, enumerated over subsets of size <= 3 plus the pairwise sums of current carries/partial results), such that for some not-yet-realized target ANF the residue O - g*h drops in algebraic degree or in monomial count; add node m = g*h to S (so later nodes may use it, which is the common-subexpression step) and continue until every O_w lies in L(S). Let A = number of AND nodes. (4) Emit the circuit: for each AND node m = g*h, build g and h onto two scratch wires with cx/x (or in place when g,h are already single wires), then and_compute(g_wire, h_wire -> anc_m) [4 T, Gidney gadget |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; realize each output wire as its linear form over S with cx/x; then walk the AND nodes in reverse and release each one with and_uncompute(anc_m) = H(anc_m), X-basis measurement, classically controlled cz(g_wire, h_wire) [0 T], undoing the cx's that built g,h just before each release so both factor wires still hold g,h at release time. Total non-Clifford cost = 4*A, independent of how many ccx/ccz the input had. Fires only if 4*A is strictly below the current cost of the segment.
cards.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form, so step (2) computes each output wire's Boolean function exactly on all inputs, and step (3)-(4) is verified against that same function: the emitted circuit's output ANF is, by construction, the linear form chosen for each wire over S, and each XAG node's value is exactly g*h because Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with no residual relative phase, so cx(anc_m -> z) acts as ccx(g,h;z) on every basis state. Linear forms are built with cx/x, which are exact permutations. Because the schedule is CHOSEN by the rule (not matched against pre-existing gate pairs), every ancilla is released at a point where its two factor wires are restored to g and h by construction; H + X-basis measurement collapses anc_m to |0> and the classically controlled CZ(g_wire,h_wire) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m*(g AND h)} phase, so each branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m for all v and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). All ancillas are clean in and out, the permutation is reproduced wire by wire, and the only freedom left is global phase. Soundness does not depend on the AND-extraction heuristic: a wrong or suboptimal factorization simply fails the final 'every O_w in L(S)' check (rule does not fire) or is caught by the judge's relaxed specification check; the heuristic only affects A, i.e. the gain.
cards.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit (or its maximal segment between the first and last ccx/ccz) that becomes Hadamard-free after folding all h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h trigrams, i.e. contains only x, cx, ccx, ccz, with >= 2 ccx/ccz gates. No family-specific pattern is required: the trigger is purely (a) Hadamard-free-after-folding, (b) step-(3) terminates with every output ANF inside L(S), and (c) 4*A < current non-Clifford cost of the segment (so it can never raise T). This is deliberately a weaker, family-blind trigger than the earlier adder-specification card, which never fired because it demanded an exact ripple-carry ANF pattern with named A/B/carry wire lists.
cards.expected_effect: adder_6's 11 ccx/ccz currently cost 11 x 4 = 44 T because the book pays one AND gadget per gate. At the function level the 6-bit sum needs only the carry chain: each carry satisfies C_{i+1} = a_i + (a_i + b_i)(a_i + C_i), one AND node per carry over signals already available (a_i, b_i, C_i), and the sum bits are pure XORs. Sequential AND extraction therefore returns A = 5 (or 6 if the carry-in wire holds a variable), i.e. 20-24 T, with the 11 ccx and 22 h all gone, replaced by ~30 cx/x, 5-6 and_compute, 5-6 measured and_uncompute (0 T) and 5-6 extra clean ancillas (14 -> ~19 qubits; T is first in the lexicographic order). Result ~20-24 T vs 44 now, far below pyzx 47 / TKET 59 / BQSKit 77. The same trigger should also reduce mcx_10 (single degree-k monomial: A = k-1 AND nodes) and reproduce the Karatsuba count on mult_4 without the bilinear special case.
cards.source: Meuli, Soeken, Roetteler, Haener, 'Xor-And-Inverter Graphs for Quantum Compilation' (npj Quantum Information 2022) and Soeken et al. 'Reducing the multiplicative complexity in logic networks for cryptography and T-count' (T-count = 4 x AND-count of an XAG); Boyar, Peralta, Pochuev, 'On the multiplicative complexity of Boolean functions' (carry-chain AND-count n-1); C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (4-T temporary AND with measurement-based uncompute).

cards.name: xag_multiplicative_complexity_resynthesis
cards.identity: Function-level resynthesis of any Hadamard-free classical segment through an XOR-AND-inverter graph (XAG), paying 4 T per AND node and 0 T for every XOR/inverter. (1) Fold every h(q) ccz(c1,c2,q) h(q) trigram into ccx(c1,c2;q) (in adder_6 all 22 h's sit in the 11 'h ccz h' trigrams); the segment is then an op list over {x, cx, ccx} = a classical reversible permutation F on the 14 wires. (2) Symbolically simulate F over GF(2): each wire w gets its output ANF O_w in the input variables (declared-clean ancillas pinned to 0). No pattern library, no adder template. (3) Build an XAG for the whole output map by sequential AND extraction over the set S of ALREADY AVAILABLE signals (initially the input variables, i.e. the GF(2)-linear span L(S) of the live wires): repeatedly search for a product g*h, with g,h in L(S) (candidate linear forms taken from the supports appearing in the remaining ANFs, enumerated over subsets of size <= 3 plus the pairwise sums of current carries/partial results), such that for some not-yet-realized target ANF the residue O - g*h drops in algebraic degree or in monomial count; add node m = g*h to S (so later nodes may use it, which is the common-subexpression step) and continue until every O_w lies in L(S). Let A = number of AND nodes. (4) Emit the circuit: for each AND node m = g*h, build g and h onto two scratch wires with cx/x (or in place when g,h are already single wires), then and_compute(g_wire, h_wire -> anc_m) [4 T, Gidney gadget |x,y,0> -> |x,y,x&y>]; realize each output wire as its linear form over S with cx/x; then walk the AND nodes in reverse and release each one with and_uncompute(anc_m) = H(anc_m), X-basis measurement, classically controlled cz(g_wire, h_wire) [0 T], undoing the cx's that built g,h just before each release so both factor wires still hold g,h at release time. Total non-Clifford cost = 4*A, independent of how many ccx/ccz the input had. Fires only if 4*A is strictly below the current cost of the segment.
cards.correctness: ANF is a unique normal form, so step (2) computes each output wire's Boolean function exactly on all inputs, and step (3)-(4) is verified against that same function: the emitted circuit's output ANF is, by construction, the linear form chosen for each wire over S, and each XAG node's value is exactly g*h because Gidney's compute-AND gadget realizes |x,y>|0> -> |x,y>|x AND y> exactly with no residual relative phase, so cx(anc_m -> z) acts as ccx(g,h;z) on every basis state. Linear forms are built with cx/x, which are exact permutations. Because the schedule is CHOSEN by the rule (not matched against pre-existing gate pairs), every ancilla is released at a point where its two factor wires are restored to g and h by construction; H + X-basis measurement collapses anc_m to |0> and the classically controlled CZ(g_wire,h_wire) cancels the measurement-induced (-1)^{m*(g AND h)} phase, so each branch m applies K_m|v> = c_m|F(v)> with the same c_m for all v and sum_m |c_m|^2 = 1 (phase consistency). All ancillas are clean in and out, the permutation is reproduced wire by wire, and the only freedom left is global phase. Soundness does not depend on the AND-extraction heuristic: a wrong or suboptimal factorization simply fails the final 'every O_w in L(S)' check (rule does not fire) or is caught by the judge's relaxed specification check; the heuristic only affects A, i.e. the gain.
cards.trigger: A dv_recon IRCircuit (or its maximal segment between the first and last ccx/ccz) that becomes Hadamard-free after folding all h-ccz-h / h-ccx-h trigrams, i.e. contains only x, cx, ccx, ccz, with >= 2 ccx/ccz gates. No family-specific pattern is required: the trigger is purely (a) Hadamard-free-after-folding, (b) step-(3) terminates with every output ANF inside L(S), and (c) 4*A < current non-Clifford cost of the segment (so it can never raise T). This is deliberately a weaker, family-blind trigger than the earlier adder-specification card, which never fired because it demanded an exact ripple-carry ANF pattern with named A/B/carry wire lists.
cards.expected_effect: adder_6's 11 ccx/ccz currently cost 11 x 4 = 44 T because the book pays one AND gadget per gate. At the function level the 6-bit sum needs only the carry chain: each carry satisfies C_{i+1} = a_i + (a_i + b_i)(a_i + C_i), one AND node per carry over signals already available (a_i, b_i, C_i), and the sum bits are pure XORs. Sequential AND extraction therefore returns A = 5 (or 6 if the carry-in wire holds a variable), i.e. 20-24 T, with the 11 ccx and 22 h all gone, replaced by ~30 cx/x, 5-6 and_compute, 5-6 measured and_uncompute (0 T) and 5-6 extra clean ancillas (14 -> ~19 qubits; T is first in the lexicographic order). Result ~20-24 T vs 44 now, far below pyzx 47 / TKET 59 / BQSKit 77. The same trigger should also reduce mcx_10 (single degree-k monomial: A = k-1 AND nodes) and reproduce the Karatsuba count on mult_4 without the bilinear special case.
cards.source: Meuli, Soeken, Roetteler, Haener, 'Xor-And-Inverter Graphs for Quantum Compilation' (npj Quantum Information 2022) and Soeken et al. 'Reducing the multiplicative complexity in logic networks for cryptography and T-count' (T-count = 4 x AND-count of an XAG); Boyar, Peralta, Pochuev, 'On the multiplicative complexity of Boolean functions' (carry-chain AND-count n-1); C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018) (4-T temporary AND with measurement-based uncompute).
